title: The sales assistant that quoted salaries
scenario:
You are an operations manager at a software company with 400 staff. IT built an internal assistant that answers questions from company documents. It runs on a vendor's file storage and search.

In the pilot, a sales rep got a salary band in an answer. The CEO asks you to review the design before the wider launch. The exhibit shows the design draft.
exhibit:
Internal assistant: design draft v1 (made-up example data)

Storage: one shared workspace and store, 5,200 files
  Sales playbooks         1,900 files   meant for: all staff
  Product docs            2,600 files   meant for: all staff
  HR files (salary bands,   700 files   meant for: HR only
  performance reviews)

Access rule (system prompt):
  "Never reveal HR files to anyone outside HR."

File lookup: the browser sends the file_id of the
  document the user picked; the server fetches it.

Phase 2: add contracts for 300 client firms, each with
  its own client portal, in the same shared store.

Pilot: 150 questions from sales staff;
  2 answers quoted a salary band.

questions.prompt: What is the main flaw in the access rule?

options.text: The rule is too short; add examples of HR questions that the model should refuse.
options.explanation: More examples may reduce leaks, but HR text still reaches the model. OpenAI's safety guide says you don't fully control what a model shares.

options.text: Repeat the rule in every user message, so that the model sees it more often.
options.explanation: Repeating the line doesn't change what the model can see. The HR files still reach it.

options.text: HR files still reach the model; a line in the prompt is not an access control.
options.explanation: Right. Decide what each user may see before retrieval, so HR text never reaches the model for a sales request.

options.text: The rule works; 2 leaks in 150 questions is a normal error rate for a pilot.
options.explanation: Two salary leaks in a small pilot is a design failure, not noise. Each leak exposes private data that can't be taken back.

questions.prompt: What is the best fix for the HR files?

options.text: Keep HR files out of the shared store, or filter by team from the user's login.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's retrieval guide supports attribute filters before search, and the filter must come from the login, not from what a user types.

options.text: Give HR files neutral titles, so that search ranks them lower for sales questions.
options.explanation: Lower ranking still lets them appear. A salary question from a sales rep would still find them.

options.text: Ask all sales staff to sign a policy that says they won't ask HR questions.
options.explanation: The pilot leak came from normal questions. A policy can't stop the assistant from returning HR text.

options.text: Keep the shared store, but block any answer that contains the word "salary".
options.explanation: A word filter misses other wording, such as "pay band" or a plain number. The HR text still reaches the model.

questions.prompt: What should change about the file lookup?

options.text: Nothing; file IDs are long random strings, so nobody can guess another user's ID.
options.explanation: IDs can be shared, copied or leaked. Anthropic's Files API page says never to accept file IDs from end users.

options.text: Keep it, but log every file ID requested, so that misuse can be found later.
options.explanation: Logs show misuse after the data is gone. The fix is to stop trusting user-supplied IDs.

options.text: Encrypt the file ID in the browser before it is sent to the server.
options.explanation: The server would still trust an ID that came from the user. Encryption doesn't check who may see the file.

options.text: Keep file IDs on the server and map each user to their files there.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's Files API page says to treat file IDs as server-side references and keep the user-to-file mapping in your application.

questions.prompt: What should phase 2 (contracts for 300 client firms) look like?

options.text: One shared store, with each client's name in the prompt so the model picks the right files.
options.explanation: That puts access in the prompt again. Other clients' contracts would still reach the model.

options.text: A separate workspace for each client, so one client's files can't reach another.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's Files API page says to create a separate workspace per tenant for hard isolation.

options.text: One shared store, filtered on a client name that the user types into the portal.
options.explanation: A user could type another client's name. Filters must come from the login, and full separation suits client data.

options.text: One shared store for now; split it later if a client reports seeing another's contract.
options.explanation: That waits for a leak of a client's contract, which can't be undone. Separate the data before launch.
